newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Q3 Special IPCA inflation index 2.19 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Q3 Special IPCA inflation index 2.19 pct.

text.p: Brazilian inflation as measured by the Special Wider National Consumers Price Index (IPCA-E) was 2.19 percent in the third quarter of 1996, a spokeswoman for the National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said.
Inflation as measured by the index was 3.16 percent in the second quarter and 3.49 percent in the first three months of this year.
The IPCA-E is a quarterly index based on the spending of families with an income of up to 40 minimum salaries and is used to calculate the Ufir index which adjusts income tax.
Results in the third quarter of this year showed a fall in inflation from 1.37 percent in July to 0.70 percent in August and 0.11 percent in September, the spokeswoman said.
Food and beverages registered the best results, with deflation of 0.27 and 0.43 percent. On the other end of the scale, housing showed the greatest rise of 6.04 percent.

Of the eleven geographical areas surveyed, highest inflation was seen in Sao Paulo at 3.06 percent and the lowest in Fortaleza of 0.66 percent. Goiania was the only other area where inflation exceeded the national average, the IBGE said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
